proposed_from.topic: Exact algebraic certification of one unseen shared row in a relational intervention. Work with finite fully observed Markovian relational SCMs, independent ground noises, type-shared finite conditional mechanisms, compatible positive rational source laws, acyclic target groundings, and one target-relevant unsupported binary context row q in [0,1]. Given the explicit dense rational target polynomial F(q) and source tables, prove the sharp set F([0,1]), compute exact algebraic endpoints by derivative-root isolation and sign comparison, and serialize common finite-noise endpoint RSCMs with polynomial-size checkable certificates. For sampled supported rows, use simultaneous rational confidence boxes and a labeled conservative occurrence-coupling inflation; do not claim exact multivariate projection. Consumer: Ejaz--Bareinboim RelationalCausalModels Experiment 6.1 N3 traffic query, whose fitted point must be accompanied by the certified sharp [0,1] range. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Repeated shared-row factorization gives F(q); exact arithmetic checked F(q)=1/4+q/2-q^3/3 with range [1/4,1/4+sqrt(2)/6], rejected the extraneous conjugate, reproduced all source assignments, and enumerated common endpoint models. A finite breakpoint construction uses at most two irrational noise masses for the unsupported row, and a maximal-coupling telescoping argument gives delta=min(1,sum_r m_r epsilon_r) for conservative whole-set coverage. Tests covered boundary/repeated roots, ties, incompatible sources, untied occurrences, output-size accounting, nuisance-vertex failure, and generic single-parameter model-checking collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove soundness, completeness, polynomial size, and checking cost for one fixed serialized certificate grammar linking derivative roots to selected endpoint values through ties, boundary coincidences, and algebraic threshold comparisons. EARLY KILL TEST: Implement an independent producer/checker for the cubic forest; it must accept both source-reproducing endpoint models and [1/4,1/4+sqrt(2)/6] while rejecting the conjugate endpoint and any certificate omitting a positive critical point. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest causal result is Ejaz and Bareinboim's complete relational identification procedure and neural extrema criterion. The strict relation is limited to fixed instances on which that procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant: the proposed theorem returns the full compatible interval and source-reproducing endpoint RSCMs. A support-condition violation alone is not used to infer failure, and constant \(F\) gives equal point identification. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim and Duarte et al. already establish general sharp polynomial-program representations, so univariate optimization itself is not claimed as new. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris already supply the root and sign machinery. The new theorem-level object is the composed causal certificate: a fixed grammar and checker whose accepted record binds the complete schema, graphs, source tables, target query, context incidence, polynomial, and serialized groundings; replays the relational factorization yielding \(F\); verifies membership in \(Mone\); certifies exhaustive feasible critical points and exact endpoint ordering including ties; and has size and checking bounds measured against the complete explicit input encoding. The statistical rung uses positivity only for prespecified representative conditioning contexts and is deliberately an outer confidence enclosure obtained by labeled occurrence coupling, not an exact multivariate projection.

seed_details.seed: A fixed skeptical certificate grammar for exact one-unseen-row relational causal bounds
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Theorem 4.3, Theorem 5.2, Corollary D.6, Section 6.1, and Appendix E.3--E.4; LiPassmorePaulson2019UnivariateCertificates, Sections 3--5
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first unresolved step is no longer root isolation alone: it is the compositional theorem that local checks for relational factorization, exhaustive derivative roots, algebraic value links, ties, and serialized endpoint models imply the global causal sharp-set claim.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to the skeptical univariate procedure of Li, Passmore, and Paulson, the first changed step is to verify that the checked polynomial and every endpoint witness have the semantics of one common type-shared relational SCM rather than merely satisfying a univariate formula.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for relational SCM certificate, exact algebraic causal bound certificate, and one-parameter reachability certificate found univariate proof procedures and parametric model checking, but no certificate language joining those algebraic clauses to relational-source reproduction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from univariate CAD because the target is a polynomial in one variable. Rebuttal: CAD certifies a polynomial assertion but does not certify the relational derivation of that polynomial, shared-row legality, source reproduction, or attaining common endpoint SCMs; those semantic clauses are the kernel.
seed_details.burned_reason: The selected fixed-scope certificate package remained incremental at D0.5; field tier requires a materially new circuit-level compiler or tied-versus-untied structural frontier.

seed_details.seed: A sharp polynomial-image theorem with common finite-noise endpoint relational SCMs
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Theorem 4.3 and Section 6.1; ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF, Theorems 2.4 and 2.8
seed_details.proof_boundary: The support theorem fixes supported rows but does not characterize the continuum of target values when exactly one type-shared row is absent. The missing direction constructs, for every \(q\in[0,1]\), one finite-noise RSCM that preserves every source law.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to canonical-SCM polynomial programming, the first changed step eliminates every response-function coordinate except a single shared conditional row and proves that repeated target occurrences must use the same scalar \(q\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for relational partial identification, unsupported relational context bounds, and shared conditional-row polynomial images found general polynomial programs and causal-order LP bounds, but no exact one-row relational image theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: tightness follows immediately by optimizing the canonical polynomial program. Rebuttal: the unrestricted canonical feasible set can untie repeated occurrences; the required common inverse-CDF construction is what proves attainability inside the type-shared independent-ground-noise class.

seed_details.seed: A conservative occurrence-coupling confidence enclosure for sampled supported rows
seed_details.anchor: DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds, Section 7 and Appendix C; EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Experiment 6.1
seed_details.proof_boundary: The source confidence event concerns shared conditional rows, whereas the target grounding may reuse one uncertain row several times. The missing proof couples target systems in topological order and counts labeled occurrences rather than distinct rows.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to Autobounds, the first changed step is to replace exact optimization over a confidence region by a uniform total-variation perturbation lemma \(\delta=\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\) that remains valid under repeated relational use.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for repeated relational mechanism uncertainty, confidence bounds for shared conditional tables, and set-identified relational inference found multinomial regions and general set-inference inversion, but not the labeled occurrence-coupling layer.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is only a union bound around existing confidence boxes. Rebuttal: the substantive step is a pathwise coupling through an acyclic relational grounding with adaptively realized contexts; counting each row once is false, and exact nuisance projection is deliberately not claimed.

seed_details.seed: Exact fixed-\(k\) semialgebraic sharp ranges for several unsupported shared rows
seed_details.proof_boundary: For \(k>1\), the first failed step is enumeration of roots of \(F'\): extrema may lie on cube faces or positive-dimensional critical loci, so exact elimination and global nonnegativity certificates must replace univariate ordering.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The destination target--method pair is fixed-dimensional relational polynomial optimization with exact elimination and SCM witnesses.
seed_details.destination_search: The scan found general polynomial programs, spatial branch-and-bound, and exact positivity certificates, but no fixed-\(k\) relational theorem with endpoint-model serialization and output-sensitive bounds.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: fixed-dimensional real algebraic geometry already gives the algorithm. Rebuttal: the algebraic image theorem is occupied, while relational witness semantics and explicit output accounting are not; nevertheless the causal increment is too diffuse for this first version.

seed_details.seed: A minimal algebraic-noise theorem for irrational sharp endpoints
seed_details.proof_boundary: Canonical finite SCMs establish finite support but do not quantify which noise masses must be algebraic when rational source laws have an irrational optimizer.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The first changed step is to sort every rational cumulative threshold against one selected algebraic optimizer and prove that only the split atom contributes two nonrational masses.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for algebraic noise SCM witnesses and irrational sharp causal bounds found no direct match.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: inverse-CDF thresholding makes the two-mass result bookkeeping. Rebuttal: it is a useful output theorem but not a sufficient standalone kernel, so it is retained only as a lemma in the selected package.

seed_details.seed: An iff frontier for when tying repeated relational occurrences changes the sharp range
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Definition 3.3 and Theorem 4.3; ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF, Equation 11
seed_details.proof_boundary: The one-row polynomial uses the diagonal \(q_1=\cdots=q_m\), whereas generic canonical relaxations optimize over the whole cube. The proposed frontier would characterize exactly when diagonal and cube extrema agree.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The destination target--method pair changes from univariate root isolation to diagonal-versus-multilinear-cube extremum equivalence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for diagonal restriction extrema of multilinear polynomials and shared-parameter Markov chains found adjacent algebraic optimization but no relational iff theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: equality can be checked by running both optimizations. Rebuttal: a structural iff condition in coefficients or occurrence hypergraphs would be new, but no sufficiently simple condition emerged in the bounded scan.

seed_details.seed: Exact rational-function bounds for a conditionally normalized relational intervention
seed_details.anchor: EjazBareinboim2026RSCM, Definition 4.1 and Proposition 4.2; DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds, Section 5
seed_details.proof_boundary: Conditioning after intervention changes \(F(q)\) into \(A(q)/B(q)\); the first changed proof step is to certify strict positivity or isolate zeros of \(B\) before derivative-root enumeration.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The destination target--method pair is exact rational-function range certification for relational conditional causal queries.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found polynomial-fractional causal programs but no one-unseen-row relational sharpness theorem with denominator components and endpoint SCMs.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: clear denominators and reuse the polynomial algorithm. Rebuttal: denominator zeros change connectedness, attainment, and admissible components; however this target is not the named traffic consumer.

seed_details.seed: A proof-carrying compiler from bounded-treewidth relational groundings to the dense target polynomial
seed_details.proof_boundary: The endpoint solver starts from a promised dense \(F\). The first changed step is exact variable elimination on the acyclic grounding while controlling intermediate degree, coefficient height, and certificate size.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relative to fraction-free parametric model checking, target-event compilation must preserve relational context sharing and attach gate identities that a causal checker can replay.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found polynomial-time univariate model checking after explicit state expansion, but no polynomial compiler in succinct relational grounding size without a width restriction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: expand the grounding into a parametric Markov chain and invoke Theorem 7. Rebuttal: expansion can be exponential; bounded treewidth may support a genuine compiler theorem, but the width parameter and certificate calculus remain open.

seed_details.seed: Exact point-identification testing by checking whether \(F\) is constant
seed_details.proof_boundary: Under the one-row reduction, identification holds exactly when all nonconstant coefficients vanish.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: The neural extrema comparison is replaced by exact coefficient equality.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair is already covered by elementary polynomial identity testing and the anchor's extrema criterion.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate because a continuous polynomial has a singleton image exactly when it is constant. The objection holds.

seed_details.seed: Exact nuisance-box projection by checking only box vertices
seed_details.proof_boundary: The proposed first step would assert that extrema over supported-row boxes occur at nuisance vertices.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: It would replace multivariate polynomial optimization by finite vertex enumeration.
seed_details.destination_search: The presolve clique construction and the example \(F(p,q)=1/4+qp(1-p)\) directly contradict the proposed reduction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: interior nuisance optima invalidate vertex enumeration. The objection holds, so exact projection is rejected and only a labeled conservative enclosure remains.
